Import and clean cohort intervals for a study

Source: R/importDataForStudy.R
getDataForStudy.Rd

Retrieve cohort data from an OMOP CDM or read local cohort intervals, then apply observation bounds, mandatory-state requirements and optional state merging. Pass the updated study environment to createTrajectories.

Usage

getDataForStudy(
  runSavedStudy = studyEnv$runSavedStudy,
  useCDM = studyEnv$useCDM,
  trajectoryDataObject = studyEnv$trajectoryDataObject,
  cdm = NULL,
  studyEnv = NULL,
  atlasStateCohorts = studyEnv$atlasStateCohorts,
  atlasTargetCohort = studyEnv$atlasTargetCohort,
  stateCohortLabels = studyEnv$stateCohortLabels,
  baseUrl = studyEnv$baseUrl,
  outOfCohortAllowed = studyEnv$outOfCohortAllowed,
  stateCohortMandatory = studyEnv$stateCohortMandatory,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = studyEnv$stateCohortPriorityOrder,
  mergeStates = studyEnv$mergeStates,
  allowedStatesList = studyEnv$allowedStatesList,
  stateCohortAbsorbing = studyEnv$stateCohortAbsorbing,
  pathToData = studyEnv$pathToData,
  mergedStateOverrides = studyEnv$mergedStateOverrides,
  webApiHeaders = NULL,
  targetEpisodeHandling = studyEnv$targetEpisodeHandling
)

Arguments

runSavedStudy

Whether to import fresh data using the analysis rules restored by a saved-study configuration.

useCDM

Whether to retrieve cohorts from the CDM. Use FALSE for a local data frame or CSV file.

trajectoryDataObject

Data frame for a local import. An explicitly supplied non-NULL object overrides the configured CSV path. Supply NULL to use the CSV path. Overrides apply to this import only.

cdm

A CDM reference created with CDMConnector.

studyEnv

Study environment returned by cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration.

atlasStateCohorts

ATLAS state cohort IDs, or local definition names without the .json extension when baseUrl is NULL. A named vector supplies the labels when stateCohortLabels is NULL. Otherwise its names must match the configured or explicitly supplied labels in order.

atlasTargetCohort

ATLAS target cohort ID, or local definition name without the .json extension when baseUrl is NULL.

stateCohortLabels

Nonblank, non-missing clinical state labels, unique ignoring case. The labels "0", "START", "EXIT" and "OUT OF COHORT" are reserved, also ignoring case.

baseUrl

OHDSI WebAPI base URL for downloading ATLAS definitions. Use NULL to read local JSON definitions.

outOfCohortAllowed

Whether to retain state records beyond the target interval's end. The target start remains the lower boundary.

stateCohortMandatory

States that every included patient must have within the retained observation bounds. NULL or character(0) imposes no requirements. Rerun import to change these requirements before generation.

stateCohortPriorityOrder

State labels ordered from highest to lowest priority, also used to resolve inherited priorities for merged states.

mergeStates

Whether to compose overlapping state intervals into states with structured membership.

allowedStatesList

Named list of allowed destinations by source state. Each source name must be unique, nonempty and non-missing.

stateCohortAbsorbing

Labels of absorbing states, also used to derive absorbing status for merged states.

pathToData

CSV path for a local import. An explicitly supplied non-NULL path overrides the configured data object. Do not explicitly supply both non-NULL local sources.

mergedStateOverrides

List of mergedState() definitions that replace selected inherited properties of merged states.

webApiHeaders

Optional named character vector of HTTP headers for this download only, for example an Authorization header. These values are never stored in the study settings. Supply them again for each fresh download. Saved studies use their embedded definitions and need no authentication.

targetEpisodeHandling

"First" (default) retains the earliest target interval per patient. "All" retains separate, nonoverlapping intervals as episodes. Names ignore case and surrounding whitespace. Requires outOfCohortAllowed = FALSE. Changing this choice requires another import.

Value

Invisibly returns NULL after a successful import. Cleaned data are saved in the study's Data directory and studyEnv is updated for generation.

Details

The selected target intervals define observation bounds. Import clips state intervals to these bounds and combines overlapping records for the same patient, episode and state. With targetEpisodeHandling = "All", each period is cleaned independently and mandatory states apply per episode. See cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration for observation and state rules.

State labels are preserved across input sources, including spaces and punctuation. CSV identifiers and labels are read as text, preserving leading zeros and literal "NA" labels. Mandatory-state labels are also literal.

Patients without state records remain eligible unless mandatory-state requirements exclude them. Discrete trajectories then use the gap rule; continuous trajectories contain only boundary markers.

An empty eligible cohort is not a successful import. Previous cleaned data, merged-state artifacts and saved settings remain unchanged. An unsuccessful import blocks trajectory generation until a later import succeeds.

Local input

With neither local source explicitly supplied, the configured data object is used when present, otherwise the configured CSV path is used. An explicit non-NULL source overrides the opposite configured source for this call only. Supplying trajectoryDataObject = NULL selects the CSV path. The same rules apply to saved local studies. CDM imports ignore both local source arguments.

Cohort definitions and saved studies

Fresh CDM imports publish downloaded definitions and their manifest only after retrieval, cleaning and saving succeed. Failed imports preserve the previous working JSON files. Local definitions and unrelated JSON files are not rewritten.

Successful CDM source overrides are retained for subsequent imports, keeping target and state selectors and the ATLAS URL aligned with clinical labels. Failed attempts retain the previous source settings. Downloaded definitions use 0.json for the target and atlas_<id>.json for states. Repeated state IDs share a file without changing their clinical labels.

After successful import and generation, the settings and cohort definitions are saved in Settings/analysisSettings.rds. Current snapshots use version 6; versions 4 and 5 load with first-period behavior. The snapshot contains no patient records.

Saved CDM runs query fresh data using the embedded definitions, leaving working JSON files unchanged. Saved local runs require fresh local input. Both restore their analysis rules without accepting overrides. See the import vignette for the saved-study workflow.

vignette("a02_import", package = "Cohort2Trajectory"), vignette("a05_output", package = "Cohort2Trajectory")

Examples

cohorts <- data.frame(
  subject_id = rep("001", 3),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "Stable", "Complication"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date("2020-01-01") + c(0, 0, 7),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date("2020-01-21")
)
folder <- tempfile("c2t-example-")
study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "example", pathToStudy = folder,
  useCDM = FALSE, trajectoryDataObject = cohorts,
  stateCohortLabels = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("Complication", "Stable"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority", cycleLength = 7
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
#> ℹ Importing data ...
#> ✔ Importing data ... [5ms]
#> 
#> ✔ Get cohort data success!
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...
#> ✔ Data cleaning completed!
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...

#> ℹ Saved cleaned data /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpfCOjE9/c2t-example-f56d6f54c1fd/example/Data/importedDataCleaned.csv
#> ℹ Cleaning data ...

#> ✔ Cleaning data ... [25ms]
#> 
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)
#> ℹ Creating batch 1!!!
#> ℹ Saved trajectory dataframe: /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpfCOjE9/c2t-example-f56d6f54c1fd/example/Data/patientDataDiscrete.csv
#> ℹ Saved settings to: /var/folders/04/_j3s9x5j6mvf0cbxxbbgy5_00000gn/T//RtmpfCOjE9/c2t-example-f56d6f54c1fd/example/Settings/analysisSettings.rds
#> ✔ Trajectories generated!
trajectories[c("subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date")]
